shloka_text: श्रुत्वा किम्पुरुषोत्पत्तिं लक्ष्मणो भरतस्तदा । आश्चर्यमिति चाब्रूतामुभौ रामं जनेश्वरम् ।। 7.89.1 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā kimpuruṣotpattiṃ lakṣmaṇo bharatastadā | āścaryamiti cābrūtāmubhau rāmaṃ janeśvaram || 7.89.1 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, किम्पुरुषोत्पत्तिं the origin of the Kimpurushas, लक्ष्मणो Lakshmana, भरतस्तदा and Bharata then, आश्चर्यमिति "this is wonderful" thus, च and, अब्रूताम् they both said, उभौ both, रामं to Rama, जनेश्वरम् the lord of people.
explanation: Having heard the origin of the Kimpurushas, Lakshmana and Bharata then both exclaimed "This is wonderful!" to Rama, the lord of people.
comments: Budha woos the woman Ila, who yields, and they pass the month happily; when Ila turns man again, Budha consoles him that his army perished in a storm and bids him stay a year -- in the ninth month the woman Ila bears Budha a son, Pururavas, while the man Ila lives on under Budha's care, woman one month and man the next.

shloka_text: अथ रामः कथामेतां भूय एव महायशाः । कथयामास धर्मात्मा प्रजापतिसुतस्य वै ।। 7.89.2 ।।
transliteration: atha rāmaḥ kathāmetāṃ bhūya eva mahāyaśāḥ | kathayāmāsa dharmātmā prajāpatisutasya vai || 7.89.2 ||
translation: अथ then, रामः Rama, कथामेतां this story, भूय again, एव indeed, महायशाः the greatly renowned, कथयामास narrated, धर्मात्मा the righteous-souled, प्रजापतिसुतस्य of the son of Prajapati, वै indeed.
explanation: Then, the greatly renowned and righteous-souled Rama indeed narrated this story again, concerning the son of Prajapati.

shloka_text: सर्वास्ता विद्रुता दृष्ट्वा किन्नरीर्ऋषिसत्तमः । उवाच रूपसम्पन्नां तां स्त्रियं प्रहसन्निव ।। 7.89.3 ।।
transliteration: sarvāstā vidrutā dṛṣṭvā kinnarīrṛṣisattamaḥ | uvāca rūpasampannāṃ tāṃ striyaṃ prahasanniva || 7.89.3 ||
translation: सर्वास्ताः all of them, विद्रुताः having fled, दृष्ट्वा having seen, किन्नरीः the Kinnaris, ऋषिसत्तमः the best among sages (Budha), उवाच spoke, रूपसम्पन्नाम् endowed with beauty, ताम् that, स्त्रियम् woman, प्रहसन् इव as if laughing.
explanation: Seeing all the Kinnaris flee, the best among sages, Budha, spoke to that beautiful woman as if laughing.

shloka_text: सोमस्याहं सुदयितः सुतः सुरुचिरानने । भजस्व मां वरारोहे भक्त्या स्निग्धेन चक्षुषा ।। 7.89.4 ।।
transliteration: somasyāhaṃ sudayitaḥ sutaḥ surucirānane | bhajasva māṃ varārohe bhaktyā snigdhena cakṣuṣā || 7.89.4 ||
translation: सोमस्य of Soma, अहम् I, सुदयितः very beloved, सुतः son, सुरुचिरानने O one with a very beautiful face, भजस्व love, माम् me, वरारोहे O beautiful woman, भक्त्या with devotion, स्निग्धेन with loving, चक्षुषा eyes.
explanation: Budha declared himself to be the beloved son of Soma and urged the beautiful woman to love him with devoted and tender eyes.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा शून्ये स्वजनवर्जिते । इला सुरुचिरप्रख्यं प्रत्युवाच महाग्रहम् ।। 7.89.5 ।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā śūnye svajanavarjite | ilā suruciraprakhyaṃ pratyuvāca mahāgraham || 7.89.5 ||
translation: तस्य his, तत् that, वचनम् speech, श्रुत्वा having heard, शून्ये in the desolate place, स्वजनवर्जिते devoid of her own people, इला Ila, सुरुचिरप्रख्यम् to the very radiant one, प्रत्युवाच replied, महाग्रहम् to the great planet (Budha).
explanation: Hearing his words in that desolate place, devoid of her own people, Ila replied to the radiant Budha, the great planet.

shloka_text: अहं कामचरी सौम्य तवास्मि वशवर्तिनी । प्रशाधि मां सोमसुत यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ।। 7.89.6 ।।
transliteration: ahaṃ kāmacarī saumya tavāsmi vaśavartinī | praśādhi māṃ somasuta yathecchasi tathā kuru || 7.89.6 ||
translation: अहम् I, कामचरी moving at will, सौम्य O gentle one, तव your, अस्मि am, वशवर्तिनी obedient, प्रशाधि command, माम् me, सोमसुत O son of Soma, यथा as, इच्छसि you wish, तथा so, कुरु do.
explanation: Ila declared herself to be free-willed but now submissive to him, asking the gentle son of Soma to command her and do as he pleased.

shloka_text: तस्यास्तदद्भुतप्रख्यं श्रुत्वा हर्षमुपागतः । स वै कामी सह तया रेमे चन्द्रमसः सुतः ।। 7.89.7 ।।
transliteration: tasyāstadadbhutaprakhyaṃ śrutvā harṣamupāgataḥ | sa vai kāmī saha tayā reme candramasaḥ sutaḥ || 7.89.7 ||
translation: तस्याः her, तत् that, अद्भुतप्रख्यम् wonderful (speech), श्रुत्वा having heard, हर्षम् joy, उपागतः attained, सः he, वै indeed, कामी desirous, सह with, तया her, रेमे enjoyed, चन्द्रमसः of the Moon, सुतः son.
explanation: Hearing her wonderful words, the son of the Moon, filled with desire, indeed rejoiced and enjoyed himself with her.

shloka_text: बुधस्य माधवो मासस्तामिलां रुचिराननाम् । गतो रमयतो ऽत्यर्थं क्षणवत्तस्य कामिनः ।। 7.89.8 ।।
transliteration: budhasya mādhavo māsastāmilāṃ rucirānanām | gato ramayato 'tyarthaṃ kṣaṇavattasya kāminaḥ || 7.89.8 ||
translation: बुधस्य of Budha, माधवः Madhava, मासः month, तामिलाम् Tamila, रुचिराननाम् with a beautiful face, गतः passed, रमयतः while enjoying, अत्यर्थम् exceedingly, क्षणवत् like a moment, तस्य for him, कामिनः the lustful one.
explanation: For Budha, the lustful one, the month of Madhava passed like a moment while he was exceedingly enjoying with Tamila of the beautiful face.

shloka_text: अथ मासे तु सम्पूर्णे पूर्णेन्दुसदृशाननः । प्रजापतिसुतः श्रीमाञ्छयने प्रत्यबुध्यत ।। 7.89.9 ।।
transliteration: atha māse tu sampūrṇe pūrṇendusadṛśānanaḥ | prajāpatisutaḥ śrīmāñchayane pratyabudhyata || 7.89.9 ||
translation: अथ Then, मासे when the month, तु indeed, सम्पूर्णे was complete, पूर्णेन्दुसदृशाननः whose face was like the full moon, प्रजापतिसुतः the son of Prajapati, श्रीमान् the glorious one, शयने on his bed, प्रत्यबुध्यत awoke.
explanation: Then, when the month was complete, the glorious son of Prajapati, whose face was like the full moon, awoke on his bed.

shloka_text: सो ऽपश्यत्सोमजं तत्र तपन्तं सलिलाशये । ऊर्ध्वबाहुं निरालम्बं तं राजा प्रत्यभाषत ।। 7.89.10 ।।
transliteration: so 'paśyatsomajaṃ tatra tapantaṃ salilāśaye | ūrdhvabāhuṃ nirālambaṃ taṃ rājā pratyabhāṣata || 7.89.10 ||
translation: सः He, अपश्यत् saw, सोमजम् the son of Soma, तत्र there, तपन्तम् performing penance, सलिलाशये in the water reservoir, ऊर्ध्वबाहुम् with raised arms, निरालम्बम् without support, तम् to him, राजा the king, प्रत्यभाषत spoke in return.
explanation: The king (Pururavas) saw Budha, the son of Soma, performing severe penance there in the water, with his arms raised and without support, and then the king spoke to him.

shloka_text: भगवन्पर्वतं दुर्गं प्रविष्टो ऽस्मि सहानुगः । न च पश्यामि तत्सैन्यं क्व नु ते मामका गताः ।। 7.89.11 ।।
transliteration: bhagavanparvataṃ durgaṃ praviṣṭo 'smi sahānugaḥ | na ca paśyāmi tatsainyaṃ kva nu te māmakā gatāḥ || 7.89.11 ||
translation: भगवन् O venerable one!, पर्वतम् mountain, दुर्गम् difficult to access, प्रविष्टः entered, अस्मि I am, सहानुगः with my followers, न not, च and, पश्यामि I see, तत् that, सैन्यम् army, क्व where, नु indeed, ते those, मामकाः my people, गताः gone.
explanation: The king addressed Budha, saying, "O venerable one, I entered this difficult mountain with my followers, but I do not see my army; where have my people gone?"

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा तस्य राजर्षेर्नष्टसञ्ज्ञस्य भाषितम् । प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यं सान्त्वयन्परया गिरा ।। 7.89.12 ।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā tasya rājarṣernaṣṭasañjñasya bhāṣitam | pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyaṃ sāntvayanparayā girā || 7.89.12 ||
translation: तत् That, श्रुत्वा having heard, तस्य his, राजर्षेः of the royal sage, नष्टसञ्ज्ञस्य whose consciousness was lost, भाषितम् speech, प्रत्युवाच replied, शुभम् auspicious, वाक्यम् words, सान्त्वयन् consoling, परया with supreme, गिरा voice.
explanation: Having heard the bewildered words of that royal sage, Budha replied with auspicious words, consoling him with a supreme voice.

shloka_text: अश्मवर्षेण महता भृत्यास्ते विनिपातिताः । त्वं चाश्रमपदे सुप्तो वातवर्षभयार्दितः ।। 7.89.13 ।।
transliteration: aśmavarṣeṇa mahatā bhṛtyāste vinipātitāḥ | tvaṃ cāśramapade supto vātavarṣabhayārditaḥ || 7.89.13 ||
translation: अश्मवर्षेण by a shower of stones, महता great, भृत्याः servants, ते your, विनिपातिताः were killed, त्वं you, च and, आश्रमपदे in the hermitage, सुप्तः sleeping, वातवर्षभयार्दितः afflicted by the fear of wind and rain.
explanation: Your servants were killed by a great shower of stones, and you were sleeping in the hermitage, afflicted by the fear of wind and rain.

shloka_text: समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते निर्भयो विगतज्वरः । फलमूलाशनो वीर निवसेह यथासुखम् ।। 7.89.14 ।।
transliteration: samāśvasihi bhadraṃ te nirbhayo vigatajvaraḥ | phalamūlāśano vīra nivaseha yathāsukham || 7.89.14 ||
translation: समाश्वसिहि be comforted, भद्रं welfare, ते to you, निर्भयः fearless, विगतज्वरः free from anxiety, फलमूलाशनः one who eats fruits and roots, वीर O hero, निवस reside, इह here, यथासुखम् as comfortably as possible.
explanation: Be comforted, may good fortune be with you; O hero, reside here fearlessly and free from anxiety, subsisting on fruits and roots as comfortably as you wish.

shloka_text: स राजा तेन वाक्येन प्रत्याश्वस्तो महामतिः । प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं दीनो भृत्यक्षयाद् भृशम् ।। 7.89.15 ।।
transliteration: sa rājā tena vākyena pratyāśvasto mahāmatiḥ | pratyuvāca tato vākyaṃ dīno bhṛtyakṣayād bhṛśam || 7.89.15 ||
translation: सः that, राजा king, तेन by that, वाक्येन word, प्रत्याश्वस्तः reassured, महामतिः great-minded, प्रत्युवाच replied, ततः then, वाक्यं words, दीनः distressed, भृत्यक्षयात् due to the destruction of servants, भृशम् greatly.
explanation: That great-minded king, though reassured by those words, then replied with great distress due to the loss of his servants.

shloka_text: त्यक्ष्याम्यहं स्वकं राज्यं नाहं भृत्यैर्विनाकृतः । वर्तयेयं क्षणं ब्रह्मन्समनुज्ञातुमर्हसि ।। 7.89.16 ।।
transliteration: tyakṣyāmyahaṃ svakaṃ rājyaṃ nāhaṃ bhṛtyairvinākṛtaḥ | vartayeyaṃ kṣaṇaṃ brahmansamanujñātumarhasi || 7.89.16 ||
translation: त्यक्ष्यामि I will abandon, अहं I, स्वकं my own, राज्यं kingdom, न not, अहं I, भृत्यैः by servants, विनाकृतः deprived of, वर्तयेयं I can live, क्षणं for a moment, ब्रह्मन् O Brahmana, समनुज्ञातुम् to permit, अर्हसि you ought.
explanation: O Brahmana, I will abandon my own kingdom, for I cannot live even for a moment without my servants; you ought to permit me to do so.

shloka_text: सुतो धर्मपरो ब्रह्मञ्ज्येष्ठो मम महायशाः । शशबिन्दुरिति ख्यातः स मे राज्यं प्रपत्स्यते ।। 7.89.17 ।।
transliteration: suto dharmaparo brahmañjyeṣṭho mama mahāyaśāḥ | śaśabinduriti khyātaḥ sa me rājyaṃ prapatsyate || 7.89.17 ||
translation: सुतः son, धर्मपरः devoted to dharma, ब्रह्मन् O Brahmana, ज्येष्ठः eldest, मम my, महायशाः very famous, शशबिन्दुः Shashabindu, इति thus, ख्यातः known, सः he, मे my, राज्यं kingdom, प्रपत्स्यते will obtain.
explanation: O Brahmana, my eldest son, who is devoted to righteousness and very famous by the name Shashabindu, will succeed to my kingdom.

shloka_text: न हि शक्ष्याम्यहं हित्वा भृत्यदारान्सुखान्वितान् । प्रतिवक्तुं महातेजः किञ्चिदप्यशुभं वचः ।। 7.89.18 ।।
transliteration: na hi śakṣyāmyahaṃ hitvā bhṛtyadārānsukhānvitān | prativaktuṃ mahātejaḥ kiñcidapyaśubhaṃ vacaḥ || 7.89.18 ||
translation: न not, हि indeed, शक्ष्यामि I am able, अहं I, हित्वा having abandoned, भृत्यदारान् servants and wives, सुखान्वितान् comfortable, प्रतिवक्तुं to reply, महातेजः O greatly effulgent one, किञ्चिदपि even a little, अशुभं inauspicious, वचः word.
explanation: O greatly effulgent one, I am indeed unable to utter even a single inauspicious word in reply, having abandoned my comfortable servants and wives.

shloka_text: तथा ब्रुवति राजेन्द्रे बुधः परममद्भुतम् । सान्त्वपूर्वमथोवाच वासस्त इह रोचताम् ।। 7.89.19 ।।
transliteration: tathā bruvati rājendre budhaḥ paramamadbhutam | sāntvapūrvamathovāca vāsasta iha rocatām || 7.89.19 ||
translation: तथा thus, ब्रुवति while speaking, राजेन्द्रे by the king of kings, बुधः Budha, परमम् exceedingly, अद्भुतम् wonderful, सान्त्वपूर्वम् consolingly, अथ then, उवाच spoke, वासः dwelling, त to you, इह here, रोचताम् may it be pleasing.
explanation: As the king of kings spoke thus, Budha, in an exceedingly wonderful and consoling manner, then said, "May your dwelling here be pleasing to you."

shloka_text: न सन्तापस्त्वया कार्यः कार्दमेय महाबल । संवत्सरोषितस्येह कारयिष्यामि ते हितम् ।। 7.89.20 ।।
transliteration: na santāpastvayā kāryaḥ kārdameya mahābala | saṃvatsaroṣitasyeha kārayiṣyāmi te hitam || 7.89.20 ||
translation: न not, सन्तापः sorrow, त्वया by you, कार्यः to be caused, कार्दमेय O son of Kardama, महाबल O mighty one, संवत्सरोषितस्य of one who has resided for a year, इह here, कारयिष्यामि I shall cause to be done, ते for you, हितम् welfare.
explanation: O mighty son of Kardama, you should not feel any sorrow, for I shall ensure your well-being here after you have resided for a year.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा बुधस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः । वासाय विदधे बुद्धिं यदुक्तं ब्रह्मवादिना ।। 7.89.21 ।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā budhasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ | vāsāya vidadhe buddhiṃ yaduktaṃ brahmavādinā || 7.89.21 ||
translation: तस्य his, तत् that, वचनं word, श्रुत्वा having heard, बुधस्य of Budha, अक्लिष्टकर्मणः of untiring action, वासाय for dwelling, विदधे he resolved, बुद्धिं mind, यत् which, उक्तं was spoken, ब्रह्मवादिना by the speaker of Brahman.
explanation: Having heard that word from Budha, whose deeds were untiring and who spoke of Brahman, Ila resolved in his mind to dwell there as instructed.

shloka_text: मासं स स्त्री तदा भूत्वा रमयत्यनिशं शुदा । मासं पुरुषभावेन धर्मबुद्धिं चकार सः ।। 7.89.22 ।।
transliteration: māsaṃ sa strī tadā bhūtvā ramayatyaniśaṃ śudā | māsaṃ puruṣabhāvena dharmabuddhiṃ cakāra saḥ || 7.89.22 ||
translation: मासं for a month, स he, स्त्री a woman, तदा then, भूत्वा having become, रमयत्य he delighted, अनिशं constantly, शुदा happily, मासं for a month, पुरुषभावेन in the state of a man, धर्मबुद्धिं righteous intention, चकार he made, सः he.
explanation: For one month, he became a woman and constantly delighted happily, and for the next month, he assumed the state of a man and focused his mind on righteousness.

shloka_text: ततः सा नवमे मासि इला सोमसुतात्सुतम् । जनयामास सुश्रोणी पुरूरवसमूर्जितम् ।। 7.89.23 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sā navame māsi ilā somasutātsutam | janayāmāsa suśroṇī purūravasamūrjitam || 7.89.23 ||
translation: ततः then, सा she, नवमे in the ninth, मासि month, इला Ila, सोमसुतात् from the son of Soma (Budha), सुतम् a son, जनयामास gave birth, सुश्रोणी (she) of beautiful hips, पुरूरवसम् Pururavas, ऊर्जितम् mighty.
explanation: Then, in the ninth month, Ila, who had beautiful hips, gave birth to a mighty son named Pururavas from Budha, the son of Soma.

shloka_text: जातमात्रं तु सुश्रोणी पितुर्हस्ते न्यवेशयत् । बुधस्य समवर्णभमिला पुत्रं महाबलम् ।। 7.89.24 ।।
transliteration: jātamātraṃ tu suśroṇī piturhaste nyaveśayat | budhasya samavarṇabhamilā putraṃ mahābalam || 7.89.24 ||
translation: जातमात्रं as soon as born, तु indeed, सुश्रोणी (she) of beautiful hips (Ila), पितुः of the father, हस्ते in the hand, न्यवेशयत् placed, बुधस्य of Budha, समवर्णभम् having a similar complexion, इला Ila, पुत्रं the son, महाबलम् very powerful.
explanation: As soon as the very powerful son, who resembled Budha in complexion, was born, Ila of beautiful hips placed him in his father Budha's hand.

shloka_text: बुधस्तु पुरुषीभूतं स वै संवत्सरान्तरम् । कथाभी रमयामास धर्मयुक्ताभिरात्मवान् ।। 7.89.25 ।।
transliteration: budhastu puruṣībhūtaṃ sa vai saṃvatsarāntaram | kathābhī ramayāmāsa dharmayuktābhirātmavān || 7.89.25 ||
translation: बुधः Budha, तु but, पुरुषीभूतं having become a man (Ila), सः he, वै indeed, संवत्सरान्तरम् after a year, कथाभी with stories, रमयामास entertained, धर्मयुक्ताभिः righteous, आत्मवान् the wise one.
explanation: But the wise Budha, after a year, entertained Ila, who had become a man again, with righteous stories. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोननवतितमः सर्गः ।। 89 ।। Thus ends the eighty-ninth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
